svg.title: Flow chart of the lecture's account of schizophrenia: three groups of risk factors, genes (70–80% heritable, exact mechanisms not yet known), prenatal factors (prenatal and maternal stress, infection, malnutrition, birth in winter or spring; maternal stress leads to serotonin and dopamine dysregulation in offspring) and postnatal factors (childhood trauma, social isolation, discrimination), feed into a neurodevelopmental disorder of genes and environment together. This leads to misfiring dopamine neurons, whose overaction causes paranoia, delusions and hallucinations (psychosis), to overactive glutamate firing in the thalamus, and over time to a loss of cells and synapses.
